# Project Design Context

## Authentication: Cobalt Mono (2026-11-09)

Latest user correction: login now shows email and password simultaneously with one submit action; only registration stays progressive. All glass input values/placeholders have 12px inline padding. Shared glass styling, pinned brand/title, internal scrolling, lossless backgrounds and five-second changes remain.

Latest viewport/login correction: the same glass step component now handles registration and login (email -> current password). Logo/title remain outside the card's internal scroll region, max-height tracks the dynamic viewport, compact spacing applies below 600px height, and automatic field focus prevents outer-page scrolling. This addresses clipping demonstrated in an 862x327 viewport. All recovery, resend, real error and guest behavior is retained. Five-second lossless slideshow remains.

Latest supplied component reference (2026-11-10): registration uses a centered glass step form with pill inputs/arrow buttons: email, password, confirmation plus required profile/consent. Adaptation lives in components/ui/sign-up.tsx; AuthCard retains actual auth actions. Real infinity brand + ArduHub, Inter, Cobalt Mono. The background interval is now explicitly 5 seconds (15-second loop). Lossless *-hq.webp assets preserve source pixels and bypass secondary image compression. Login/recovery keep their existing form flow.

Latest 2026-11-10 illustration correction replaces seated workbench scenes with a tool run (walking, reaching, parts trolley, looking out a window), collaborative giant humanoid robot construction, and the first robot test (reaching, crouching, jumping). Keep the full-screen crossfade and centered form. New assets are mentor-tool-run.webp, mentor-giant-robot.webp and mentor-robot-test.webp; exact prompts are outputs/auth-workshop/dynamic-poses-prompts.md.

2026-11-10 correction supersedes the split layout below: a full-screen workshop slideshow now sits behind a centered form. Three scenes (robotics, soldering, evening circuit/robotic arm work) crossfade over a 36-second loop, with approximately 2.2 seconds per dissolve. No workshop text, auth subtitles, role descriptions or duplicate signup prompts. Essential labels, consent, parent guidance and actions remain. Reduced motion shows the first scene; hidden tabs pause; images load before animation starts. New sources and prompts: outputs/auth-workshop/slideshow-prompts.md.

Explicit user request applies Inter and Cobalt Mono to `/sign-in`, `/register` and the shared recovery shell. The existing AuthCard behavior is retained. A single workshop illustration uses the four original mentor references: Shina soldering, Rezik assembling Arduino, Oma observing, Volt waving. Wide layouts pair the sticky workshop with a white form; narrow layouts retain the complete illustration above the form. Scoped tokens live in sign-in/auth.css, new Russian copy in src/content/ru.ts. Dark theme preserves blue accents. Generated illustration source and prompt are in outputs/auth-workshop; the 355 KB WebP is public/images/auth/mentor-workshop.webp. This supersedes the earlier statement that authentication retains its original palette.

## Public landing: Cobalt Mono (2026-11-08)

The `/` route now uses `src/app/landing-video.css` and the scoped `.landing-video` container. Latest user instruction replaces the previous floating-component hero and long galleries with a Neuralese-inspired compact video structure: blue-to-white hero with scrolling Arduino code and component names (Ludr reference), large overview video, three alternating video rows with blue/pink/green frames, four colorful benefit cards, centered FAQ and final CTA. Inter and Cobalt Mono remain. Only own local ArduHub recordings are published, explicitly labeled as example interfaces. VideoFrame owns lazy sources, automatic visibility playback, errors and reduced motion. Per user request, hero and videos have no play/pause overlay buttons. The user-supplied iridescent Glass Button material in src/app/glass-buttons.css is scoped ONLY to the first hero screen and navbar (.landing-video :is(.hero, .header)); lower landing sections also use their previous button styling. Cabinet, authentication, lessons and editor retain their previous button styling. Existing FAQ, header, footer and Reveal primitives are reused.

## ArduHub G2 constraints

The supplied docs/ArduHub_G2_ui_for_kids.md governs the child-facing dashboard. Preserve ArduHub palette and fonts, existing primitives, truthful progress, large touch targets and reduced motion. Mentor entry points belong only to learning. Full constraints are in design.json.
